doc_verification.detail: Reachability: page live (WebFetch domain-blocked in this sandbox; retrieved via web reader — full page content returned, canonical URL confirms https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/distributed/cluster-telemetry). Version: URL path v-1-18-x and page header 'v1.18.x' match target v1.18.0 (same 1.18 series). Content: doc documents verbatim 'timeout integer Optional >=1 Defaults to 60' — exactly the range constraint's assertion 'timeout default 60, minimum 1'; only documented response is 200 'Retrieved' with the telemetry payload (example body shows result.cluster.enabled=true, number_of_peers=1 — i.e. even a single-peer deployment is documented to return 200); no 4xx/5xx and no distributed-mode/cluster-enabled precondition is documented anywhere on the page. Endpoint: GET /cluster/telemetry under the Distributed tag — matches contract endpoint_registry path 'cluster+telemetry' and the raw_knowledge-derived URL used by the script. This is REST API reference (curl examples), not SDK documentation.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: HTTP 200 with telemetry payload (id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota)
contract_grounding.note: Binding provenance (moved out of the constraint_id field so it stays a bare ID): qdrant_behavioral_cluster_telemetry_001 is the violated face; the dispatched candidates.jsonl row carried constraint_id="" and the script docstring declared qdrant_range_cluster_telemetry_001 as the targeting constraint — its value-side is compliant. Violates-declaration self-check applied honestly with a constraint-citation change: w.r.t. the script's declared range constraint (verbatim assertion: "timeout default 60, minimum 1") the attack value is genuinely COMPLIANT (1000000 >= 1; the OpenAPI schema at openapi/openapi-cluster.ytt.yaml:28-35 and the live doc both specify minimum 1 and NO maximum), so the range assertion is not violated. The violated constraint is the behavioral 200-promise: a legal request to GET /cluster/telemetry returned HTTP 500 with body {"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Could not get telemetry from cluster"}} instead of the documented 200 — the doc page documents ONLY the 200 'Retrieved' response, with an example showing number_of_peers=1. Caveat for the auditor: per sibling log boundary_cluster_telemetry_001 the 500 occurs identically for omitted/default/min timeout, so the violation is deployment-conditional (standalone) and input-independent — it is NOT triggered by timeout=1000000 specifically; the verdict line's causal framing ('timeout=1000000 -> crash marker') is a misattribution, and the 'internal error' crash-marker hit is a substring of Qdrant's ordinary handled-500 envelope ('Service internal error: {description}', lib/storage/src/content_manager/errors.rs:21), not a panic/OOM signature. Behavioral description field verbatim: "returns 200 TelemetryData; internal/ops-oriented endpoint".

Break 2 (attribution, for the auditor): the verdict line attributes the 500 to the resource-limit value timeout=1000000 and calls the body text a 'crash marker', but sibling log boundary_cluster_telemetry_001 shows the identical 500 for omitted/default/min timeout — the value is not causal and the marker is the ordinary handled-error envelope; the underlying phenomenon (GET /cluster/telemetry unconditionally 500 in standalone) is real, stable across 13 scripts, and contradicts the documented 200-only contract.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /cluster/telemetry -> actix get_cluster_telemetry (cluster_api.rs:203) -> actix_web_validator Query<ClusterTelemetryParams> [range(min=1) on timeout: line 45 — 0 => 422, non-digit/overflow => serde 400 'Deserialize error in query parameters'] -> default unwrap_or(60s) (:236) -> all_peers = keys(channel_service.id_to_address) (:238-243) -> per-peer gRPC GetTelemetryRequest{timeout} (:250-256) -> internal get_telemetry converts timeout to Duration wait budget (qdrant_internal_api.rs:108, telemetry.rs:127 tokio::time::timeout — a wait budget cannot crash and the observed failure was instant) -> standalone deployment (settings.cluster.enabled=false, main.rs:479) means init_channel_service (main.rs:299) never populates id_to_address (ChannelService::new default empty, channel_service.rs:47) -> all_peers empty -> zero futures -> telemetries empty -> resolve_telemetries -> newest_telemetry(&[]) = None -> StorageError::service_error('Could not get telemetry from cluster') (distributed_telemetry.rs:157-158) -> rendered as 500 'Service internal error: ...' (errors.rs:21). Deterministic, instant (~0.14ms), input-independent on any standalone deployment; the timeout value plays no role in this path.
source_grounding.note: The contract-required input validation IS present in source: min 1 via #[validate(range(min = 1))] (live-confirmed by sibling 422 for timeout=0), default 60 via unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GRPC_TIMEOUT=60s), and all malformed/overflow streams cleanly 400'd in this very log. So the observed 500 is NOT a missing-validation defect and NOT a crash: it is an explicitly constructed handled service error on the empty-telemetries path, reached unconditionally in standalone deployments (empty id_to_address). by_design_in_source is NOT justified: no comment/docstring declares standalone-unsupported for telemetry — the only related annotation is the TODO at cluster_api.rs:24 ('TODO(cluster telemetry): Handle lower levels', about details_level) and the main.rs:284 doc comment describing the single-node channel-service shape, neither of which declares the 500 intended. The residual genuine signal: the doc (and the repo's own openapi/openapi-cluster.ytt.yaml:13-36, which documents only the 200 DistributedTelemetryData response with timeout minimum 1 default 60) promises 200 with no distributed-mode precondition, while the implementation structurally 500s on every standalone deployment — a deployment-conditional doc/impl gap, input-independent, NOT the value-triggered runtime crash the verdict claims.
